verses.1: After this, he left Athens and went to Corinth.
verses.2: And he found a Jew named Akylan, of Pontic origin. He quickly left Italy and brought his wife Priskilla with him. They decided to separate all the Jews from Jerusalem. Then he came to them.
verses.3: And because they were colleagues, he was also considered among them. After all, they were all actors in this art form.
verses.4: In addition, meetings were held every Saturday within the organization. Jews and Greeks were also involved in these meetings.
verses.5: And those who came from Macedonia, namely Silas and Timothy, were also included in Paul’s message. He warned the Jews that Jesus Christ was indeed the Son of God.
verses.6: However, when they resisted and spoke insulting words, he took out his sword and said to them, “Your blood will flow onto your heads. But I am pure. From now on, I will go among the nations.”
verses.7: And after going there, he entered the house of a man named Titius Iustus, who respected the gods. His house was located in the same neighborhood as the other houses.
verses.8: But the chief priest believed in this man with all the people in his house. Many of the Corinthians also believed and baptized themselves after hearing about him.
verses.9: And the Lord said to Paul during the night through a vision: “Do not be afraid. Instead, speak out and do not remain silent.”
verses.10: For I am with you, and no one will attack you in any way. After all, I have a great following in this city.
verses.11: He spent six years and months teaching them the words of God.
verses.12: And because Galianus was a man from Achaea, the Jews became like-minded with Paul. They invited him to their gathering.
verses.13: They say that by this law, he teaches people to respect the God.
verses.14: And when Paul was about to open the door, Gallio said to the Jews, “If there was any injustice or wrongdoing, I will deal with you according to the law.”
verses.15: But if the matter relates to words, names, and laws as they apply to you, then let them decide that. I do not want to be the judge in these matters.
verses.16: And he kept them away from that place.
verses.17: All of them took Sothén as the leader of the group, right at the beginning of their journey. And they didn’t pay any attention to anything related to this Frenchman at all.
verses.18: And Paul, with only a few days left before he was ready to leave for Syria, went there along with Priscilla and Aquila. He stayed in Cilicia, as he had requested.
verses.19: They remained in Ephesus, and he ignored them. He went into the assembly and appointed the Jews as leaders.
verses.20: But he refused to allow them to stay with him for a longer period of time.
verses.21: But after arranging everything, I say: Once again, I return to you, in accordance with the will of God. He was removed from Ephèse.
verses.22: And after going to Caesarea, he went up and took control of the congregation there. Then he went down to Antiochia.
verses.23: And after some time had passed, he departed, traveling through the regions of Galatia and Phrygia, while supporting all his students along the way.
verses.24: There was also a Jew named Apollos, who was of Alexandrian origin. He was a wise man. He was appointed to serve in Ephesus, as he was very skilled in writing.
verses.25: He was the one who learned the path of the Lord. With his divine spirit, he accurately taught about Jesus. He truly understood everything related to Jesus, and he knew all about John’s baptism.
verses.26: And he began to act arrogantly in the assembly. When Priscillus and Acutus heard this, they took him away from there, and they made sure that he would no longer be able to act arrogantly.
verses.27: As they wanted him to go to Achaea, his brothers wrote to the disciples, asking them to welcome him. When he arrived, he caused great joy among those who heard him speak.
verses.28: For the Jews, it was publicly proven through the writings that Jesus Christ was indeed the Messiah.
